title: Habit-stack portfolio lab — personal OKR scratchpad
content:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is my running personal OKR / habit-stack scratchpad. Not polished; rough, iterative, intentionally fragmentary. Primary goal: get a small set of measurable habits and experiments that increase my sustained deep-focus time, shipping predictability on small infra tasks, and awareness of cost/latency tradeoffs for the models/features I touch.

Why separate?
- Drive docs are fast and disposable; use here to capture micro-decisions, measurement tweaks, and failed/partial experiments before baking into Confluence.

Top-level objective (Q4 personal): increase reliable weekly high-focus output by 40% while avoiding burnout.

Draft OKRs (working):
O1: Improve weekly deep-focus throughput and predictable delivery cadence.
KR1.1: Average 12 focused hours/week (tracked as calendar blocks) by end of Q4 — current baseline 8.2h.
KR1.2: Reduce midweek context-swaps (interruptions) to <4/week measured by unscheduled meetings & ad-hoc pings.
KR1.3: Ship 6 small deliverables (infra PRs, consoles, docs) with self-reported quality >= 4/5.

O2: Make data-driven micro-optimizations to Redwood-serving experiments I touch.
KR2.1: Run 3 micro-experiments (batching, kv-cache config, quant profile) with clear metric to track (latency p95, cost/token).
KR2.2: Achieve at least one config that reduces cost-per-1000-tokens by >8% without degrading median latency >10ms.

Measurement plan / primitives I track here (quick defs):
- Focus hour = 1 continuous 50+ minute blocked calendar item labeled "focus" with notifications off.
- Interrupt = unscheduled Slack message that requires me to stop focus block.
- Deliverable = merged PR with description + release note; small = <8 files changed.
- Experiment record = short note: hypothesis, variant, metric, baseline, result.

Weekly snapshot template (copy into weekly entries below):
- Week start date: 
- Focus hours: 
- Interrupts: 
- Deliverables: 
- Experiments launched/observed: 
- Mood/energy quick note: 
- Key blockers: 
- 1 micro-action for next week: 

---

Week snapshots (running)

Week start: 2024-10-07
- Focus hours: 7.0
- Interrupts: 9 (high)
- Deliverables: 1 (cli-tunables PR)
- Experiments: 0
- Mood: meh — lots of meetings clumped
- Blockers: meeting-heavy Tuesday/Wednesday
- Next micro-action: schedule two 90-min no-meeting blocks Tue/Thu morning

Week start: 2024-10-14
- Focus hours: 8.5
- Interrupts: 5
- Deliverables: 0 (blocked on infra review)
- Experiments: 1 (small batching toggle on staging)
- Mood: better, clearer output Fri afternoon
- Blockers: slow reviews
- Next micro-action: pair-review slot Wed 10-11am

Week start: 2024-10-21
- Focus hours: 9.0
- Interrupts: 4
- Deliverables: 2 (kb update + perf test harness)
- Experiments: 1 (batching) — result: staging p95 latency +6ms, token-cost -5% at current load; hypothesis partially validated
- Mood: optimistic
- Blockers: hard to isolate traffic patterns for stable measurement
- Next micro-action: add trace tags to track request size distribution

Week start: 2024-10-28
- Focus hours: 9.8
- Interrupts: 3
- Deliverables: 1 (canary rollout of batching config)
- Experiments: 0 (follow-up monitoring)
- Mood: good, energy stable
- Blockers: noisy baseline due to traffic spike
- Next micro-action: coordinate with SRE on quiet window for controlled run

Observations so far (raw notes):
- Batching improves cost but p95 sensitivity to tail events is real. Need to triage by request-size buckets.
- Meetings cause fractional context swaps more than total meeting count; 1-hour meetings right after focus blocks are worst.
- Pair-review slot helped unblock PRs and sped reviews by ~1 day on average.

Micro-experiments log (short):
1) Batching factor +1 in staging (2024-10-14). Hypothesis: small increase reduces token cost by >3% for our sequence distribution. Metric: cost/1k tokens, median latency, p95 latency. Result: cost -5%, median latency unchanged, p95 +6ms. Conclusion: promising but need tail mitigation.
2) KV-cache preload (2024-11-01). Hypothesis: pre-populating cache for high-volume routes reduces token regen and p50 latency. Metric: stall frequency, p50. Status: ongoing, sampling only.
3) Meeting-free mornings (2024-10-22 personal experiment). Hypothesis: 2x 90-minute morning blocks increase focus hours. Result: focus hours up ~15% week-over-week; subjective mood improved.

Personal habit stack (what I try to keep consistent):
- Wake + 20m walk, no phone (anchor)
- 2x 90-min morning focus blocks (deep work)
- Lunch walk + 15m reading (reset)
- End-of-day 15m triage & task-list for next day
- Weekly Friday retro 30m (plan + one micro-experiment)

Failures / things to avoid (notes):
- Trying to optimize too many experiments at once -> noisy results.
- Overloading review requests the same day as major meetings.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do I formalize these personal OKRs into a lightweight Confluence page? Pros: easy reference and shareable with manager. Cons: overhead + premature formalization.
- What is the right cadence for cost experiments? Weekly is noisy; monthly may be too slow. Consider "bursty" windows when traffic is low for controlled runs. Need SRE coordination.

Action backlog (short):
- [ ] Create small Confluence stub if manager asks (LOW priority)
- [ ] Add trace tags to API to split requests by prompt size (HIGH)
- [ ] Book recurring Wed 10-11 pair-review slot with infra-team (MED)
- [ ] Coordinate a 2-hour controlled traffic window with SRE (MED)
- [ ] Harden experiment measurement: add zapper dashboard for p50/p95/cost-per-1k at request-size buckets (HIGH)

Ideas for scaling this into a repeatable system (brain dump):
- Personal OKR dashboard: weekly auto-ingest from calendar + PR merges + experiment labels. Small Lambda to compile weekly snapshot that I can paste into Confluence.
- Shared team micro-experiment board: quick one-line records so pattern matching across experiments becomes possible (e.g., batching always increases tail under X conditions).

Notes to self (loose):
- Keep the habit stack light; the leverage is in consistent 2–3 anchors, not dozens of small rituals.
- When an experiment is ambiguous, immediately (within 48h) change only one variable.

Reference links (quick):
- Redwood Console guide (personal notes): https://redwood.internal/console-guide (private stub)
- Relevant PR: GH-PR-6789 (small batching change)
- SRE related ticket: LINEAR-9402

End — will update weekly. This doc is disposable; if an item stabilizes, move it to Confluence.
